header:
Synthesis of Weinreb Amides
Since their discovery, N-methoxy-N-methylamides have been widely known as Weinreb amides (WAs). WAs exhibit reactivity distinct from that of ordinary amides: they can serve both as excellent acylating reagents and as aldehyde equivalents and are important building blocks in numerous organic syntheses.

subquestions.text_open: 9.1 The most common method for preparing Weinreb amides is condensation of a carboxylic acid with N,O-dimethylhydroxylamine. Because amide condensation is thermodynamically unfavorable, an additional coupling reagent is usually required. The carboxylic acid below is to be condensed with N,O-dimethylhydroxylamine to prepare an N-protected amino-acid WA. 9.1.1 DCC is selected as the coupling reagent. Write the SMILES strings of one key intermediate and the coproduct (the product other than the Weinreb amide).

9.1.2 Experimentally, using DCC alone gives a product racemized at the stereogenic carbon because the intermediate in Question 9.1.1 is further converted into a cyclic intermediate that undergoes isomerization and causes racemization. Write the SMILES string of the cyclic intermediate and draw the isomerization mechanism.

9.2 A trichloromethyl carbinol can undergo a homologation-amination reaction to form a WA containing one additional carbon, as shown below. 9.2.1 Under these conditions, $\mathrm{(PhSe)_2}$, $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$, and EtOH generate a complex anion X that contains an Se-B bond but no B-H bond and may be regarded as an equivalent of $\mathrm{PhSe^-}$. Write the equation for formation of anion X.

9.2.5 The experiment also produces a byproduct whose molecular mass is approximately 30 lower than that of the major product. Replacing the methyl group bonded to O in N,O-dimethylhydroxylamine with another group can markedly suppress formation of this byproduct, although the reaction time increases accordingly. Using the relevant information, write the SMILES string of one possible modified substrate.
